paragraphs: Morning light fills my small old shop, where every piece of [[stuff:stuff]] and second-hand [[merchandise:merchandise]] holds a past life.
A girl walks in with a worn travel [[souvenir:souvenir]] and a [[clay:clay]] [[artifact:artifact]] her kind grandmother left her.
I check the [[raw:raw]] wood and the [[crude:crude]] joints [[first:first]], then plan each [[gentle:gentle]] repair [[step:step]].
Warm coats are a winter [[necessity:necessity]], so I decide to repair her torn [[festival:festival]] [[outfit:outfit]] today.
I open my repair [[kit:kit]] and lift each little chrome [[utensil:utensil]] with slow care.
People call such things roadside [[rubbish:rubbish]], yet I [[reuse:reuse]] them and turn them into gifts full of warmth.
This bent board once lay in a [[junk:junk]] pile beside the old city [[landfill:landfill]].
Street [[sewerage:sewerage]] work had left it under a coat of [[dust:dust]], so I washed it with a [[mild:mild]] [[detergent:detergent]].
A caregiver drops by with hand [[lotion:lotion]] and a low wide [[tub:tub]] for soaking dirty cloth.
I [[pull:pull]] out the little [[plug:plug]] and turn on the old [[tap:tap]] to rinse the [[frame:frame]] clean.
A short zinc [[pipe:pipe]] and a soft [[hollow:hollow]] [[tube:tube]] hold the legs firmly together.
Before starting work, I clean the floor with a wet [[mop:mop]] and an old [[straw:straw]] [[broom:broom]].
An old man then brings in a thin torn [[mattress:mattress]] and a dusty rolled-up [[carpet:carpet]].
His small flowered [[rug:rug]] and door [[mat:mat]] both need fresh edges and a brighter color.
I fill each [[flat:flat]] seat [[cushion:cushion]] with a soft [[feather:feather]] [[pad:pad]] so it feels comfortable again.
His baby's blue [[blanket:blanket]] and the cherished wedding [[quilt:quilt]] both smell of long years in the sun.
I wash the yellowed [[pillow:pillow]] and scrub its marks away with a soft [[sponge:sponge]].
Then I dry it with a thick white [[towel:towel]] and clip its label back on with one small [[staple:staple]].
I pull out each old [[nail:nail]] and cut away the loose edges with a sharp [[razor:razor]].
Each [[rough:rough]] corner is [[shave:shaved]] [[smooth:smooth]], and the faulty safety [[fuse:fuse]] is replaced with a new one.
A black power [[cable:cable]] and a long white [[cord:cord]] hang quietly behind the desk.
I twirl each loose wire [[strand:strand]] into place, then light a small honey-scented [[candle:candle]].
Warm [[wax:wax]] drips softly while I read repair tips from an old [[paperback:paperback]].
A picture [[pamphlet:pamphlet]] shows old crafts, and I keep the small parts wrapped in soft [[tissue:tissue]].
I [[xerox:xerox]] the old invoice, then put the short [[memorandum:memorandum]] up on the wall above my desk.
My drawer of old [[stationery:stationery]] looks messy, yet the strong [[glue:glue]] still works well.
Blue [[ink:ink]] marks my notebook while a thick [[rubber:rubber]] [[band:band]] holds the pages together.
With a pair of large silver [[scissors:scissors]], I [[shear:shear]] the loose threads from the thick cloth along the white line.
The [[round:round]] chair [[rim:rim]] is loose, but every carved [[element:element]] stays truly beautiful.
Cost is only one small [[factor:factor]], so I repair just the worst-damaged [[section:section]].
I shine his old school [[badge:badge]] and tighten each tiny silver [[bolt:bolt]].
A [[round:round]] door [[knob:knob]] and a curved drawer [[handle:handle]] also need a [[gentle:gentle]] fixing today.
The battered window [[shutter:shutter]] shakes in the wind, while the long flowered [[curtain:curtain]] hangs still.
I change the cracked window [[pane:pane]], for its cloudy [[opacity:opacity]] blocks the warm light.
Buttons sleep in a glass [[jar:jar]], and old hooks rest inside a small [[barrel:barrel]].
I carry water in a red [[bucket:bucket]] and rinse my brushes in a little enamel [[pail:pail]].
The shop [[phone:phone]] rings twice, and then the little door [[bell:bell]] sings merrily.
My [[portable:portable]] lamp is handy, but the strong [[spotlight:spotlight]] shows up every defect.
The old [[paper:paper]] [[lantern:lantern]] glows softly again after I change its little warm [[bulb:bulb]].
My pocket [[flashlight:flashlight]] helps me peer behind the humming old [[refrigerator:refrigerator]].
The small [[fridge:fridge]] keeps humming while I clean up the [[dust:dust]] with the loud [[vacuum:vacuum]].
A worn delivery [[hurdle:hurdle]] and a fallen garden [[fence:fence]] wait for repair behind the shop.
I oil the loose bike [[pedal:pedal]] and straighten the long leaning wall [[shelf:shelf]].
Then I [[climb:climb]] my short red [[ladder:ladder]] to reach the tall three-legged [[painting:painting]] [[stool:stool]] in the corner.
By the door, a torn black [[umbrella:umbrella]] and a yellowed child's [[raincoat:raincoat]] keep [[drip:dripping]].
I [[dredge:dredge]] the thick mud from the bottom of the old well and [[pour:pour]] it into a rusty enamel [[can:can]].
The old [[mill:mill]] has closed down, so I warm the joints at a neighbor's small [[forge:forge]].
This light [[alloy:alloy]] [[frame:frame]] feels softer than pure [[metal:metal]].
An old [[flat:flat]] [[iron:iron]] stands beside a shining candlestick of yellow [[brass:brass]].
A small green [[bronze:bronze]] [[horse:horse]] sits next to a bag of grey [[cement:cement]].
White powdered [[lime:lime]] and [[smooth:smooth]] wall [[plaster:plaster]] repair the cracked corner nicely.
A cracked brown [[leather:leather]] bag and a clear [[plastic:plastic]] cover are waiting for their turn.
Each plant [[fibre:fibre]] feels [[rough:rough]], while the soft blue [[fabric:fabric]] feels [[smooth:smooth]].
Grandma loves to [[knit:knit]] warm caps, and I [[weave:weave]] the torn seat anew.
A thick painted [[canvas:canvas]] and white table [[linen:linen]] cover the worktop.
Soft white [[cotton:cotton]] shirts and a strong blue [[nylon:nylon]] bag hang outdoors to dry.
Freshly cut [[lumber:lumber]] smells sweet, and every [[wooden:wooden]] leg shines after oiling.
A date [[pit:pit]] lies near the heater, where wood is our [[steady:steady]] winter [[fuel:fuel]].
I [[lubricate:lubricate]] each stiff hinge, then hang up a clear shining [[crystal:crystal]] pendant.
No [[inferior:inferior]] parts stay in this shop, and every [[counterfeit:counterfeit]] coin goes back to the man who brought it.
A [[fake:fake]] pearl breaks fast, for its thin painted shell is quite [[fragile:fragile]].
A [[miniature:miniature]] model chair is the only gift still [[available:available]] today.
Strong seams make each repair [[durable:durable]], and that slowly wins me [[popularity:popularity]] among the neighbors.
Short capes are in [[vogue:vogue]], but warm snugness will always [[prevail:prevail]] here.
A young [[idol:idol]] loves [[plain:plain]] dress, not the flashy [[luxury:luxury]] of the shops.
No [[extravagant:extravagant]] spending is needed when old family [[jewellery:jewellery]] shines anew.
Each tiny bright [[jewel:jewel]] and polished blue [[gem:gem]] glows in the little dish on my table.
A pale green [[jade:jade]] ring will [[adorn:adorn]] the cover of the old music box.
Every little gold [[ornament:ornament]] will [[embellish:embellish]] the [[plain:plain]] [[festival:festival]] dress.
I [[embroider:embroider]] red flowers while my sister practises [[gentle:gentle]] wedding [[hairdressing:hairdressing]] on a young bride.
[[natural:Natural]] green [[pigment:pigment]] and a safe brown [[dye:dye]] give the pale cloth its color.
For the [[spring:spring]] [[masquerade:masquerade]] dance, she wears a thin shining [[veil:veil]].
Her old dance [[costume:costume]] will [[fascinate:fascinate]] every child in the front row.
A [[decent:decent]] clean hem looks good, and neat buttons add an [[exquisite:exquisite]] touch.
She walks with [[gentle:gentle]] [[grace:grace]] and a [[quiet:quiet]], simple [[elegance:elegance]] every day.
Her neat new [[appearance:appearance]] needs no costly shop [[cosmetics:cosmetics]] at all.
Light soft [[makeup:makeup]] keeps her looking sweet and [[charming:charming]] all day long.
We [[clothe:clothe]] the child warmly and repair every torn school [[garment:garment]].
The freshly folded [[laundry:laundry]] fills the small [[wardrobe:wardrobe]] in her tidied bedroom once more.
His work [[overall:overalls]] are covered in dust, so he borrows a long grey [[overcoat:overcoat]].
A soft morning [[robe:robe]] and a long evening [[gown:gown]] hang behind the screen.
I repair a blue winter [[sweater:sweater]] and a brown biking [[jacket:jacket]].
His grey work [[trousers:trousers]] need a strong button and a little silver [[clasp:clasp]].
I shape the bent hat [[brim:brim]] and wash a soft flowered [[scarf:scarf]].
A white dotted [[handkerchief:handkerchief]] and a small buttoned [[purse:purse]] lie side by side.
I keep a worn brown [[wallet:wallet]] and a grey sleeveless [[vest:vest]] for daily use.
I [[wrap:wrap]] the gift neatly and hang her dark theatre [[cloak:cloak]] inside the cupboard.
The white shirt [[collar:collar]] is bent, and one [[sleeve:sleeve]] of the long coat is too short.
One warm winter [[sock:sock]] and a thin party [[stocking:stocking]] still wait for their matching pairs.
Her pink soft [[slipper:slippers]] are worn through, yet the white [[lace:lace]] edging still looks pretty.
The kind old [[tailor:tailor]] will [[sew:sew]] the hem before the evening show.
We [[spin:spin]] the yarn smoothly and add one strong hidden [[stitch:stitch]].
My sharp chrome [[needle:needle]] flashes, and each colored [[pin:pin]] holds a pleat in place.
A long red [[string:string]] and a thin white [[thread:thread]] lie beside the roller.
A torn bag [[strap:strap]] hangs loose, while a painted wall [[stripe:stripe]] guides my cut.
A pink satin [[ribbon:ribbon]] ties the box shut, and a black school [[belt:belt]] needs new holes.
A thin gold [[chain:chain]] shines beside her small new [[bracelet:bracelet]].
Her old pearl [[necklace:necklace]] broke, so I renew the silk and reset every tiny fallen [[bead:bead]].
The [[textile:textile]] scraps I saved and a piece of red [[velvet:velvet]] fill the little box.
Soft grey [[wool:wool]] and a flowered knee [[patch:patch]] save the old coat.
I wipe the worktop with a torn cleaning [[rag:rag]] here in our [[shabby:shabby]] but cozy corner.
The [[tight:tight]] [[belt:belt]] is eased, and a calm deep [[purple:purple]] shade hides the repair.
A soft [[tan:tan]] coat is cleaned with care, so its warm color will never [[fade:fade]].
Each dark food [[stain:stain]] and each paint [[blot:blot]] slowly fades from the cloth.
The tall singer is quite a [[figure:figure]] on our street today, looking [[slender:slender]] in her fixed dress.
At [[dusk:dusk]] we share tea, thankful for each [[slight:slight]] repair that warms our street.
Grandma announced her plan for the [[erection:erection]] of a new hall, brushing aside every past [[stricture:stricture]] about money.
Mom agreed to [[construct:construct]] a warm dining hall, though old [[dust:dust]] might [[obstruct:obstruct]] or even [[ruin:ruin]] dinner.
Mingming wanted to [[establish:establish]] clear duties for everyone, starting with washing the grey [[concrete:concrete]] floor.
Uncle Wang brought bright [[steel:steel]] tools, promising strength and long [[stability:stability]] for the shelves.
They walked around the dusty [[site:site]], dreaming of how the future [[venue:venue]] would welcome guests.
The old house was a village [[landmark:landmark]], quietly [[situated:situated]] beside green trees and [[narrow:narrow]] paths.
Mom tried to [[locate:locate]] the old drawings in the corner where grandpa once chose to [[reside:reside]] and cook.
Small birds still [[inhabit:inhabit]] the roof, but they will [[migrate:migrate]] elsewhere once the noise begins.
Grandma decided to [[settle:settle]] downstairs, keeping the whole [[dwelling:dwelling]] [[lively:lively]] day and [[night:night]].
Mingming joked that their home was no [[skyscraper:skyscraper]] and no rich man's [[villa:villa]], yet it was full of love.
Unlike a cold [[mansion:mansion]] or a crowded [[apartment:apartment]], this place kept childhood memories alive.
They refused to turn it into a noisy [[hostel:hostel]] or a hunting [[lodge:lodge]] for strangers.
Behind the yard stood a weak [[hut:hut]] and a [[wooden:wooden]] [[cabin:cabin]] full of battered chairs.
Mom opened the dark [[cellar:cellar]] and the leaning [[shed:shed]], coughing through the thick [[dust:dust]].
The little [[cottage:cottage]] next door once served as a daytime [[nursery:nursery]] for village children.
Mingming found his tiny [[cradle:cradle]] there, now a safe [[shelter:shelter]] for the kittens.

Mingming joked that the old house had no [[escalator:escalator]], gripping the loose [[wooden:wooden]] [[handrail:handrail]] tightly.
Grandma wiped one stone [[pillar:pillar]] after another, counting each tall [[column:column]] aloud.

Mom praised the [[round:round]] [[arch:arch]] and the high [[ceiling:ceiling]] that kept the summer air cool.
Sparrows nested under the wide [[eaves:eaves]], near the tall stone [[chimney:chimney]] full of soot.
They planned a simple [[reception:reception]] corner, brighter than any hotel [[lobby:lobby]] in town.

Grandma kept the stone [[fireplace:fireplace]] but removed the rusty [[iron:iron]] [[radiator:radiator]] beside it.
Mingming cleaned the dusty [[living room:living room]] shelves, polishing every [[wooden:wooden]] [[cabinet:cabinet]] door.
Mom opened the sunny [[balcony:balcony]] doors and swept dry leaves off the stone [[terrace:terrace]].

Uncle Wang scrubbed the yellowed [[toilet:toilet]] seat, then wiped the stained edge of the [[bath:bath]] [[tub:tub]].
Unlike the noisy town [[mall:mall]] or the stone shopping [[complex:complex]], home felt calm.

Nobody wanted a flashy [[casino:casino]] or a noisy photo [[studio:studio]]; they longed for warm meals.
Though the town grew more [[urban:urban]] every year, their own alley stayed [[quiet:quiet]] and almost [[peripheral:peripheral]], like a dream.
Shops in the near [[vicinity:vicinity]] closed early, leaving the [[night:night]] street an empty [[void:void]].
After we cleared away the [[junk:junk]], the hall looked [[spacious:spacious]] yet still dusty, far from [[airtight:airtight]] and safe.
Mingming ran across the wide [[expanse:expanse]] toward the small front [[plaza:plaza]], shouting with joy.
He imagined the house as a storybook [[castle:castle]], and then the old [[carpenter:carpenter]] appeared.
The careful [[mason:mason]] tapped each loose floor [[tile:tile]], humming an old village [[tune:tune]].
By [[sunset:sunset]], fresh grey [[brickwork:brickwork]] along the doorway promised many busy mornings ahead.
Mingming woke with a sharp [[appetite:appetite]], eager to help Mom [[cater:cater]] for tomorrow's guests.
They checked the stored food, keeping only fresh [[edible:edible]] things as a [[provision:provision]] for the week.

Unlike the school [[refectory:refectory]] or the noisy street [[bar:bar]], home food would be [[gentle:gentle]] and warm.

Mingming carried a [[wooden:wooden]] [[tray:tray]] and a [[mug:mug]] of warm milk without spilling a drop.

Uncle Wang checked the old [[stove:stove]] flames and cleaned the cold brick [[furnace:furnace]] behind it.

Uncle Wang hid his [[whisky:whisky]] bottle and his sweet [[brandy:brandy]] away from the children.

Grandma threw away a wet [[cigarette:cigarette]] end, keeping her head clear and [[sober:sober]].
At [[dawn:dawn]] they picked green [[pea:pea]] pods and crisp long [[cucumber:cucumbers]] in the garden.

Mingming pulled up orange [[carrot:carrots]] and [[flat:flat]] white [[turnip:turnips]] from the soft soil.

Mom taught him to [[strip:strip]] off wilted leaves and keep the soft yellow [[core:core]] inside.
They cracked open the [[rough:rough]] [[seed:seed]] [[hull:hull]], tasting one red wild [[berry:berry]] after another.
Mingming traded two bunches of [[purple:purple]] [[grape:grapes]] for two soft, sweet [[papaya:papayas]].
Grandma dried red [[plum:plum]] slices in the sun, thanking the autumn [[crop:crop]] for its lavish gifts.
Uncle Wang carried golden ears of [[corn:corn]] and heavy [[grain:grain]] sacks into the yard.
They ground the pale [[wheat:wheat]] kernels, remembering how farmers [[reap:reap]] under the hot sun.
Mom mixed white [[flour:flour]] with water and cooked thick morning [[porridge:porridge]] for everyone.
Mingming stirred the sticky rice [[paste:paste]], watching the village [[livestock:livestock]] crowd up to the fences.

Uncle Wang netted a silver [[fish:fish]] from the clear [[pond:pond]] behind the bamboo grove.

Mingming tasted the thick white [[yogurt:yogurt]] and spread soft yellow [[butter:butter]] on his bread.

Grandma twirled the long [[spaghetti:spaghetti]] into little nests and chilled sweet milk [[pudding:pudding]] for dessert.
Mingming crunched a square [[biscuit:biscuit]] and spread red strawberry [[jam:jam]] thick on his bread.

Mom passed round the strong yellow [[mustard:mustard]] and a tiny dab of green [[wasabi:wasabi]] with care.
Uncle Wang crushed the black [[pepper:pepper]] grains and sliced the pale yellow [[ginger:ginger]] [[root:root]] thinly.
Mingming minced the white [[garlic:garlic]] cloves and long green [[scallion:scallions]] for the soup.

Grandma loved the [[mild:mild]] [[fruit:fruit]] [[flavour:flavour]], not the sharp [[sour:sour]] taste of unripe plums.
Mingming spat out the [[bitter:bitter]] skin and reached for the warm soup instead, [[mild:mild]] and [[spicy:spicy]].
The guests called the stew [[delicious:delicious]] and said the warm buns were simply [[yummy:yummy]].
The hot noodles were [[tasty:tasty]], just right for [[thirsty:thirsty]] workers after a long day.
Mom ground red [[spice:spice]] powder, simmering a thick tomato [[sauce:sauce]] slowly.
Mingming squeezed wavy lines of red [[ketchup:ketchup]], while the roses nearby gave off [[natural:natural]] [[perfume:perfume]].
Grandma counted every fresh [[ingredient:ingredient]], adding a herbal health [[supplement:supplement]] for the elders.

Uncle Wang helped [[fry:fry]] golden potato shreds, then watched Grandma [[roast:roast]] chestnuts slowly.
They served crisp morning [[toast:toast]], warning the children not to [[suck:suck]] the hot soup too fast.
Mingming learned to [[swallow:swallow]] his food calmly, refusing to [[lick:lick]] his fingers at the table.

Mom told him to [[soak:soak]] the dried mushrooms, then briefly [[dip:dip]] the greens in boiling water.
Grandma taught Mingming to [[squeeze:squeeze]] oranges and gently [[stir:stir]] honey into his tea.
At last Mom began to [[grind:grind]] sesame seeds, and the yard filled with a nutty fragrance.
They hung the [[paper:paper]] lamps on thin [[suspension:suspension]] cords, tying each [[knot:knot]] to an [[iron:iron]] [[hook:hook]].
Mingming pulled the [[wooden:wooden]] [[lever:lever]], steadying the tall bamboo [[scaffold:scaffold]] for his uncle.

When the old fan showed signs of [[malfunction:malfunction]], the neighbors started a [[lively:lively]] [[debate:debate]] about repairs.
Grandma asked Uncle Wang to [[fix:fix]] the wires and carefully [[mend:mend]] the torn tablecloths before daybreak.
Mom chose to [[modify:modify]] the menu, asking Mingming to [[trim:trim]] the wilted flowers neatly.
Uncle Wang began to [[weld:weld]] the chair legs, while Mingming held the sharp [[saw:saw]] [[steady:steady]].

They used a model of a small earth [[dam:dam]], learning how workers [[assemble:assemble]] bridges together.
Workers came to [[install:install]] bright lamps and [[furnish:furnish]] the corners with flowers and stools.
Mingming admired the neat [[placement:placement]] of the bowls and the [[clever:clever]] table [[layout:layout]].

Children played [[outside:outside]] the doorway, then ran [[outward:outward]] toward the music and laughter.

Grandma led the tours through the [[inner:inner]] rooms, showing off the renewed [[interior:interior]] with pride.

sentZh: 晨光洒满我的旧小店，这里每件旧物、每件二手商品都藏着一段过去。
一个女孩走进店里，带来一件磨损的旅行纪念品，还有她慈祥奶奶留下的一件陶土手工艺品。
我先检查生木料和粗糙的接缝，再为每一步轻柔的修补做好计划。
保暖外套是冬天的必需品，所以我决定今天补好她那件撕破的节日套装。
我打开修补工具箱，小心地拿起每一件小小的镀铬用具。
人们管这些东西叫路边垃圾，可我把它们重新利用，做成满是暖意的礼物。
这块弯木板原先躺在旧城填埋场边的一堆废旧杂物里。
街道排污施工让它蒙上了一层灰，于是我用了温和的洗涤剂把它洗净。
护理员顺路送来护手乳液和一只泡脏布用的矮宽盆。
我拔掉小塞子，拧开旧水龙头，把框架冲洗干净。
一截短锌管和一根软空心管把桌腿牢牢固定在一起。
动工之前，我先用湿拖把和旧草扫帚把地面打扫干净。

velvet.m: n. 天鹅绒；丝绒；adj. 天鹅绒的
velvet.ex: The chair has a soft velvet cover.
velvet.exZh: 这把椅子有柔软的丝绒坐垫。

venue.m: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场
venue.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
venue.exZh: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。

vest.ex: He wears a black vest over his shirt.
vest.exZh: 他穿着一件黑色背心，上面是衬衫。

viaduct.ex: The train goes over a long viaduct.
viaduct.exZh: 火车驶过一座长长的高架桥。

vicinity.ex: The park is in the vicinity of my house.

villa.ex: They live in a big villa near the sea.
villa.exZh: 他们住在海边的一座大别墅里。

vinegar.ex: He put vinegar on his salad.

vogue.ex: Blue jeans are in vogue this year.

void.ex: The void on the page made the text look empty.
void.exZh: 页面上的空白让文字看起来空荡荡的。

wallet.ex: He lost his wallet on the bus.
wallet.exZh: 他在公交车上丢了钱包。

wardrobe.ex: He put his clothes in the wardrobe.

wax.ex: Bees make wax to build their hives.

weave.ex: She weaves a basket from reeds.
weave.exZh: 她用芦苇编织一个篮子。

weld.ex: He welds metal pieces together with a torch.
weld.exZh: 他用焊枪把金属片焊接在一起。

wheat.ex: Farmers grow wheat in the field.

wooden.ex: He sat on a wooden chair.
wooden.exZh: 他坐在一张木制椅子上。

wool.ex: She knits a sweater from wool.

wrap.ex: She bought a warm wrap for the winter.
wrap.exZh: 她买了一件保暖的包裹（披肩）过冬。

xerox.m: v. 复印；n. 施乐复印机（商标名称）
xerox.ex: He used the xerox to copy his resume.
xerox.exZh: 他用施乐复印机复印了他的简历。

yogurt.ex: I eat yogurt for breakfast every day.
